label: input token r during the original phase (positions 0-6)
explanation: Token detector for the letter r as an input in the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It fires on essentially every r at original positions 0-6 and never on any other token. Magnitude is highest when r is the first token (about 1.0 of max) and around 0.77-0.89 at later positions. A repeated r, i.e. not the first occurrence in the sequence, gives a much weaker activation (often about 0.1-0.3). It is silent at the <DEL> step and on r at original positions 7-8. In the copy phase it fires only weakly and rarely (about 0.1% of mass), on r fed back as a copy input.

issues: The predicate holds up. On test: precision 1.0, recall 0.974, F1 0.987, mass recall 0.9985. It fires on no token except r, and the false-positive list is empty on both dev and test.

The test misses do not form a systematic class. There are 2673 missed steps holding 0.1% of the mass. Most are r at orig_idx 7, which is active 35% of the time but very weakly (about 0.03-0.17 of max, mass recall 0.0009). The rest are weak copy-phase r (about 0.02-0.09). Neither depends on L (precision at idx 7 is 0.33 for L=8 and 0.36 for L=9) or on in_first.

The explanation says a repeated r is 'much weaker (often about 0.1-0.3)'. That is wrong. Repeated r at orig_idx<7 (in_first==0) makes up 8.1% of active steps and 6.4% of the mass, so its mean is about 0.79x the overall mean, not a small fraction of it. Dev examples of repeated r: 0.59, 0.91 (r r at the start), 0.91, 0.36, 0.60, 0.16, 0.09. The values vary a lot; only some are weak.

Saying it is 'silent on r at positions 7-8' is a slight overstatement: r at idx 7 fires on 35% of occurrences, though weakly. The claim that the copy phase is rare and weak is correct: phase==2 & r has precision 0.008 and mass 0.05%. The claims that it is silent at <DEL> and peaks at the first position are correct (orig_idx 0 holds 23% of the mass on 16% of active steps).
